findings.source_quote: We now live in an easier place; the Southern Highlands of Tanzania.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate or localize the region name into standard contemporary Italian and preserve meaning. For example: “le Highlands meridionali della Tanzania” or “l'altopiano meridionale della Tanzania”. Replace the English phrase but keep it inside the same paragraph and tags.
findings.translation_quote: Ora viviamo in un luogo più facile: le Southern Highlands della Tanzania.

findings.location: ...Fa freddo (45 degrees or less in the morning).
findings.source_quote: It’s cold (45 degrees or colder in the morning).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the original numeric temperature wording but avoid implying a unit change. Either keep the original ambiguous wording (e.g. “45 degrees o meno”) or specify the unit as in the English source only if known. Suggested fix: “Fa freddo (45 gradi o meno al mattino).” If the publication uses Celsius, add “(45 °F/≈7 °C)” only if the editor confirms unit conversion. Implement the change inside the same paragraph and tags.
findings.translation_quote: Fa freddo (45 gradi o meno al mattino).

findings.source_quote: There are peace lilies, roses, hibiscus, and other bright flowers blooming, and succulents growing in delightful little pots.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the Italian name of 'peace lilies' to a standard contemporary form. Replace “spatafilli” with “spatifilli” (or “spathiphyllum/spatifillo” per houseplant usage). Keep the rest of the sentence unchanged and inside the same paragraph and tags.
findings.translation_quote: Ci sono spatafilli, rose, ibischi e altri fiori vivaci in fiore, e piante succulente che crescono in deliziosi vasetti.
